pack.description: Cross-disciplinary academic vocabulary: the words used to describe research, argue a point and report evidence in any field.
pack.selection_note: Internal high-yield selection of words that recur across all academic subjects; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: to study something carefully in order to understand it or explain it
entries.example_academic: Researchers analyzed twenty years of rainfall records to identify the trend.

entries.definition: a particular way of dealing with a problem or doing something

entries.definition: to judge the quality, amount or importance of something

entries.definition: to accept that something is true without having proof

entries.definition: to limit the size, amount or range of something
entries.example_academic: The law restricts the sale of antibiotics without a prescription.
entries.example_spoken: The library restricts access to that room after nine.

entries.definition: to keep something or continue to have it
entries.example_academic: Clay soils retain water far longer than sandy ones.
entries.example_spoken: I read the chapter twice but retained almost nothing.

entries.definition: to use one thing or person in place of another
entries.example_academic: Producers substituted cheaper materials when prices rose.
entries.example_spoken: You can substitute yogurt for cream in this recipe.

entries.definition: based on general ideas rather than on real things or events
entries.example_academic: The discussion remained abstract and offered no practical recommendations.
entries.example_spoken: That's too abstract for me; can you give an example?

entries.definition: to gradually get more of something over time, or to increase gradually
entries.example_academic: Toxins accumulate in the bodies of animals at the top of the food chain.
entries.example_spoken: I've accumulated way too many open tabs.

entries.definition: next to or very near something
entries.example_academic: Samples were taken from the forest and from adjacent farmland.
entries.example_spoken: The parking lot is adjacent to the gym.

entries.definition: to officially give something, such as money or time, to a particular purpose or person
entries.example_academic: Only two percent of the budget was allocated to research.
entries.example_spoken: We allocated ten minutes to each speaker.

entries.definition: similar in some way to another thing, so that a comparison is useful
entries.example_academic: The wing of a bat is analogous to the human arm.
entries.example_spoken: It's analogous to learning to drive: awkward at first, then automatic.

entries.definition: to expect something and prepare for it
entries.example_academic: Planners failed to anticipate the growth in car ownership.
entries.example_spoken: I didn't anticipate so many questions after my talk.

entries.definition: not based on a reason, system or plan, and therefore seeming unfair or random
entries.example_academic: The boundary between the two categories is somewhat arbitrary.
entries.example_spoken: The word limit seems totally arbitrary.

entries.definition: to happen at the same time as something else, or to be the same
entries.example_academic: The rise in literacy coincided with the spread of cheap newspapers.
entries.example_spoken: My exam coincides with my sister's wedding.

entries.definition: to reduce the bad effect of something, or to pay someone for a loss
entries.example_academic: Higher yields compensated for the loss of farmland.
entries.example_spoken: Nothing can compensate for a bad night's sleep before an exam.

entries.definition: to combine well with something and make it more complete or effective
entries.example_academic: Field observations complement the data collected by satellite.
entries.example_spoken: The two courses complement each other really well.

entries.definition: to form an idea or plan in the mind; to imagine something
entries.example_academic: The canal was conceived as a way of bypassing the rapids.
entries.example_spoken: I can't conceive of doing all that in one week.

entries.definition: to keep someone or something within the limits of a particular place, activity or subject
entries.example_academic: The discussion is confined to the period before the reform.
entries.example_spoken: Please confine your comments to the topic.

entries.definition: to be different from what is usual or expected; to move away from a plan
entries.example_academic: Actual spending deviated sharply from the original estimate.
entries.example_spoken: He never deviates from his morning routine.

entries.definition: separate and clearly different from other things of the same kind
entries.example_academic: The process can be divided into four discrete stages.
entries.example_spoken: Think of it as three discrete tasks, not one big one.

entries.definition: to force something or someone out of its usual place, or to take its place
entries.example_academic: Factory production gradually displaced household weaving.
entries.example_spoken: The new dorm displaced the old tennis courts.

entries.definition: to change something so that it is no longer true or accurate, or no longer has its normal shape
entries.example_academic: Subsidies distort prices and encourage overproduction.
entries.example_spoken: The microphone distorts my voice.

entries.definition: including many different types of people or things
entries.example_academic: The reef supports an extraordinarily diverse community of fish.
entries.example_spoken: Our class is really diverse; there are students from twenty countries.

entries.definition: more important, powerful or noticeable than other things of the same type
entries.example_academic: Agriculture remained the dominant sector of the economy until the 1950s.
entries.example_spoken: English is the dominant language in the lab.

entries.definition: to include a large number or range of things
entries.example_academic: The term encompasses a wide variety of farming systems.
entries.example_spoken: The course encompasses everything from grammar to public speaking.

entries.definition: to involve something as a necessary part or result
entries.example_academic: Any expansion of the port would entail the loss of wetlands.
entries.example_spoken: What exactly does the internship entail?

entries.definition: stated clearly and exactly, leaving nothing to be guessed
entries.example_academic: The contract makes no explicit reference to overtime.
entries.example_spoken: The professor was explicit: no late submissions.

entries.definition: suggested or understood without being stated directly
entries.example_academic: There is an implicit assumption that all firms have equal access to credit.
entries.example_spoken: There was an implicit criticism in her question.

entries.definition: to include something as part of a larger whole
entries.example_academic: The revised model incorporates data on rainfall and soil type.
entries.example_spoken: I incorporated your comments into the second draft.

entries.definition: certain to happen and impossible to avoid
entries.example_academic: Given the scale of the debt, some form of default was inevitable.
entries.example_spoken: A few mistakes are inevitable when you speak fast.

entries.definition: to make something begin
entries.example_academic: The ministry initiated a review of safety procedures.
entries.example_spoken: She initiated the conversation, not me.

entries.definition: to become involved in a situation in order to change what happens
entries.example_academic: The central bank intervened to stabilize the currency.
entries.example_spoken: The resident advisor had to intervene in the argument.

entries.definition: fair, reasonable or allowed by law
entries.example_academic: Critics raised legitimate concerns about the reliability of the data.
entries.example_spoken: That's a legitimate question, and I don't have the answer.

entries.definition: seeming likely to be true or reasonable
entries.example_academic: A more plausible explanation is that the tools were traded, not made locally.
entries.example_spoken: His excuse sounded plausible, so I let it go.

entries.definition: happening before something more important, as a preparation or first stage
entries.example_academic: Preliminary results suggest that the treatment is safe.
entries.example_spoken: These are just preliminary ideas; nothing is decided.

entries.definition: very careful and thorough, with high standards
entries.example_academic: The drug underwent rigorous testing before it was approved.
entries.example_spoken: It's a rigorous program, so expect a lot of work.

entries.definition: to provide information that supports a statement or theory
entries.example_academic: Tree-ring data corroborate the written accounts of the drought.
entries.example_spoken: Can anyone corroborate your story?

entries.definition: to make something clear by explaining it more fully
entries.example_academic: The experiment helped to elucidate the role of the enzyme.
entries.example_spoken: Could you elucidate what you mean by "soon"?

entries.definition: to make a bad situation or problem worse
entries.example_academic: The drought exacerbated tensions between farmers and herders.
entries.example_spoken: Skipping meals will only exacerbate your headaches.

entries.definition: to make something less harmful, serious or painful
entries.example_academic: Planting trees along the river mitigated the effects of flooding.
entries.example_spoken: A good outline mitigates the risk of running out of time.

entries.definition: showing awareness of small but important differences in meaning or opinion
entries.example_academic: A more nuanced account recognizes that the reform had winners and losers.
entries.example_spoken: Her answer was more nuanced than a simple yes or no.

entries.definition: a typical pattern or model of something; a set of ideas that shapes how a subject is understood
entries.example_academic: The discovery overturned the dominant paradigm in the field.
entries.example_spoken: Remote work is a completely different paradigm.

entries.definition: to suggest that something is true as a starting point for reasoning
entries.example_academic: The theory postulates the existence of particles that have never been observed.
entries.example_spoken: He postulated that the noise came from the pipes.

entries.definition: to prevent something from happening or make it impossible
entries.example_academic: The poor condition of the bones precludes any firm conclusion about diet.
entries.example_spoken: A part-time job doesn't preclude you from applying.

entries.definition: to claim to be or do something, especially when this may not be true
entries.example_academic: The document purports to be a letter written by the king himself.
entries.example_spoken: The site purports to offer free textbooks, but it's a scam.

entries.definition: to prove that a statement or theory is wrong
entries.example_academic: Later experiments refuted the claim that the effect was universal.
entries.example_spoken: I couldn't refute his argument, even though I disliked it.

entries.definition: to provide evidence that proves something is true
entries.example_academic: The author fails to substantiate the claim with any figures.
entries.example_spoken: You need to substantiate that point with a source.

entries.definition: not certain or fixed, and likely to change later; done without confidence
entries.example_academic: The authors offer a tentative explanation that requires further testing.
entries.example_spoken: We have a tentative plan to meet on Thursday.

entries.definition: to support or form the basis of an argument, theory or system
entries.example_academic: Three assumptions underpin the model, and each can be questioned.
entries.example_spoken: Trust underpins every good study group.

entries.definition: completely clear and without any possibility of doubt
entries.example_academic: The evidence for human influence on the climate is unequivocal.
entries.example_spoken: Her answer was an unequivocal no.

entries.definition: so weak, slight or uncertain that it hardly exists
entries.example_academic: The link between the two events is tenuous at best.
entries.example_spoken: That's a pretty tenuous excuse for missing the meeting.

entries.definition: an opinion or idea formed without enough evidence; a guess
entries.example_academic: The origin of the manuscript remains a matter of conjecture.
entries.example_spoken: That's pure conjecture; we don't know why she left.

entries.definition: a division into two things that are presented as completely different or opposite
entries.example_academic: The dichotomy between nature and nurture is now regarded as misleading.
entries.example_spoken: It's a false dichotomy: you can work hard and still sleep.

entries.definition: to estimate something unknown by extending what is already known
entries.example_academic: It is risky to extrapolate from a single city to the whole country.
entries.example_spoken: You can't extrapolate from one bad quiz to the whole semester.

entries.definition: to put two things next to each other in order to show how they differ
entries.example_academic: The exhibition juxtaposes ancient pottery with contemporary sculpture.
entries.example_spoken: The article juxtaposes two students' very different experiences.

entries.definition: according to what is stated or appears to be true, though the real situation may be different
entries.example_academic: The tax was ostensibly temporary, yet it remained in force for forty years.
entries.example_spoken: He came ostensibly to return a book, but he stayed two hours.

entries.definition: directly related to the matter being considered
entries.example_academic: The committee asked several pertinent questions about funding.
entries.example_spoken: That's a pertinent point; let's add it to the slides.

entries.definition: a natural tendency to behave in a particular way
entries.example_academic: Younger investors show a greater propensity to take risks.
entries.example_spoken: He has a propensity to volunteer for everything.

entries.definition: false or not genuine, although seeming to be real or true
entries.example_academic: The apparent link between the two variables turned out to be spurious.
entries.example_spoken: That's a spurious argument, and you know it.

entries.definition: more than is needed or wanted; unnecessary
entries.example_academic: The final chapter is largely superfluous and repeats earlier arguments.
entries.example_spoken: Cut the superfluous words and your email will be clearer.

entries.definition: to describe or mark something precisely, especially its limits
entries.example_academic: The report delineates the responsibilities of each agency.
entries.example_spoken: We should delineate who does what before we start.
